# A thin-edge active cap bundle forces an unused source parity

This note isolates an actual geometric source-count consequence of the thin-edge obstruction. The right-hand fiber is allowed to vary, and is not assumed to equal the left endpoint fiber. Three actual active caps, together with zero outside strip coarea, force every possible second source into an exposed fiber of insufficient volume. This is a restricted parity-budget lemma, not a general OC argument.

## 1. Precise statement

Let n=1 and d=4. Let T be a 4-simplex of volume V with barycentric coordinates lambda_0,...,lambda_4. Put

    D_delta={x in T: lambda_2+lambda_3+lambda_4<=delta},
    0<delta<1/5.

Let C be ANY full-dimensional compact convex body whose sampled fibers satisfy

    K_-1=D_delta,    K_0=T.

Assume all nonempty sampled fibers have positive four-dimensional volume. Use the actual pooled within-fiber covariance norm Gamma and the uniform outward smoothing kernel Psi(t)=min(1,max(0,1+t)), with parameter 0<h<1/100.

Assume that Y0=(0,y0) is an actual deepest mark in the attained smooth problem, with the usual proper own core and full-normal stationarity identity. Suppose there are three ACTUAL active caps, indexed by i=2,3,4, with affine through-source margins

    m_i(z,x)=a_i z+f_i(x),  f_i(y0)=0,

that satisfy:

1. Their continuous margins are normalized by a positive scale so that

       sup_{x in T}|f_i(x)-(lambda_i(x)-1/5)|<=1/200.

2. Their smoothed integrands vanish identically on D_delta at base -1.

3. Each of these three caps has zero transition-strip coarea on every other sampled fiber.

Then zero is the ONLY deepest integer base. In particular the actual deepest set does not occupy both integer parities.

The normalization in item1 is merely a positive rescaling of the cap equation; it rescales Gamma and the width together and leaves the smoothed cap unchanged. No arbitrary coordinate transformation is used.

## 2. Two elementary consequences of convexity

For any linear functional L on continuous coordinates, the fiber maximum H_L(t)=max_{x in C_t}L(x) is concave on the projection interval, and the fiber minimum l_L(t)=min_{x in C_t}L(x) is convex. This follows by taking maximizers or minimizers in two fibers and applying convexity of C to their weighted averages.

Every barycentric coordinate has minimum zero on both D_delta and T: D_delta contains the edge with vertices 0 and1, and for each of the two high coordinates one of those two vertices gives zero. Therefore, for every t>=0 in the projection,

    min_{C_t}lambda_k>=0,  k=0,...,4.

Indeed the secant slope of the convex minimum function between -1 and0 is zero, so its subsequent values are at least zero. Since the barycentric sum is one in the full continuous affine space, all such fibers lie in T.

There is also no sampled fiber at any integer t<=-2. Write R=lambda_2+lambda_3+lambda_4. Its minimum is zero on D_delta and T, so convexity of the minimum function gives min_{C_-2}R>=0 if that fiber exists. Its maxima at -1 and0 are delta and1, so concavity gives max_{C_-2}R<=2delta-1<0. This contradiction excludes -2, and the interval nature of the projection excludes every smaller integer as well.

## 3. A putative second source is at base1 and forces a small fiber

The standard positive-width deepest-set property gives

    conv(I) intersect Z = I,

and forbids any nontrivial convex interpolation among deepest marks at an integer base. In one integer dimension any two deepest bases must therefore be adjacent. The only possibilities in addition to zero are -1 and1.

Base -1 is exposed because no smaller integer fiber exists. A sufficiently large finite base tilt isolates its entire fiber, giving depth at most

    |D_delta|=(4delta^3-3delta^4)V< (4/125)V<Gamma_4 V.

On the other hand, the middle simplex centroid supplies raw depth at least Gamma_4 V: every halfspace through it contains that much middle volume, and outward smoothing only increases capture. Thus -1 cannot be deepest.

Suppose base1 is deepest. Each actual cap at Y0 strictly misses the mark of this different deepest source, by the full-normal kernel-centroid identity. By item3 and connectedness of the interior of K1, its smoothed integrand is constant zero or one there. The strict missed-source margin excludes one. Continuity gives zero on the whole closed K1.

Let w_i=h Gamma(grad f_i)>0 be the width in the scaling of item1. Since both the base -1 and base1 fibers are missed, their maximal margins satisfy

    max_D f_i-a_i<=-w_i,
    max_K1 f_i+a_i<=-w_i.

The edge vertex e0 belongs to D and has lambda_i(e0)=0 for i=2,3,4. The uniform approximation gives max_D f_i>=-1/5-1/200. Hence

    max_K1 f_i<=1/5+1/200-2w_i.

We already know K1 lies in T. Applying the lower approximation f_i>=lambda_i-1/5-1/200 there yields

    lambda_i(x)<=2/5+2/200=41/100,
    x in K1, i=2,3,4.                                (1)

This is an exact consequence of the two missed fibers. The nonnegative width term only strengthens the bound.

## 4. Exposure and the exact volume deficit

The coordinate maximum at base zero is one, while its maximum at base1 is at most41/100. If base2 existed, concavity of that maximum would give

    max_K2 lambda_2<=2(41/100)-1=-9/50.

But Section2 gives min_K2 lambda_2>=0. Hence base2, and every larger integer, is absent. The putative K1 is therefore an exposed sampled fiber.

By (1), K1 lies in the part of T on which three specified barycentric coordinates are at most b=41/100. Inclusion-exclusion computes its maximal possible relative volume:

    |K1|/V <= 1-3(1-b)^4+3(1-2b)^4
            =63962845/100000000 <2/3.                 (2)

Here a single event lambda_i>b is a translated homothetic simplex of volume fraction(1-b)^4, a pair has fraction(1-2b)^4, and the triple is empty because3b>1. This proves (2) without numerical integration.

We need a uniform upper bound for smooth depth rather than replacing it by ordinary halfspace depth. Choose the continuous functional lambda_2 at an arbitrary mark in K1. For the two opposite orientations, the sum of the outward integrands is at most

    1+1_{|lambda_2-lambda_2(y)|<=w},
    w=h Gamma(grad lambda_2).

All sampled fibers now lie in T, so each within-fiber variance of lambda_2 is at most1/4 and their pooled variance is at most1/4. Thus w<=h/2. The lambda_2 marginal of uniform T has density4(1-s)^3 V on[0,1], bounded by4V; the displayed slab therefore has volume at most8wV<=4hV. At least one of the two own smoothed caps has mass at most

    |K1|/2+2hV < V/3+V/50 <Gamma_4 V.                (3)

Each of those own caps can be isolated from all other sampled fibers by a sufficiently large finite positive base tilt, since base1 is exposed. Consequently (3) is an upper bound on the actual mixed smooth depth at every mark of K1. It contradicts the raw global lower bound Gamma_4 V.

There is no second deepest base. This proves the statement.

## 5. Scope of the source-count consequence

The audited thin-edge all-menu obstruction satisfies the three cap hypotheses for sufficiently small delta and h: its three complementary vertex cones miss D_delta, all outside coareas vanish, and their normalized margins converge to the canonical simplex margins. The lemma shows that this particular source cap pattern would itself prevent a new right-hand deepest source even if that right-hand body were changed, as long as the cap pattern and zero-coarea properties persisted.

This is not a theorem that positive saturation deficit always forces an unused source parity. The exact full-parity four-interval calibration in `candidate 47e23345c657e546` disproves that stronger inference. Nor is it a statement about arbitrary lower-dimensional shared patches. The continuous simplex facet constraints and the three actual near-canonical missed caps provide the needed quantitative volume deficit here.
